_why: The 47 legislature websites that will answer us, walked a few hours a night instead of in one four-and-a-half-day sitting. Brendan: 'at a reasonable, orderly pace, spread over the nightly job — days or weeks, it's free.' That is the right shape for this work twice over. It is polite: nobody's webmaster sees a machine hammering their site for four days straight, they see a slow trickle that stops every morning. And it is honest about the arithmetic — the walk is ~483,000 documents at one request per second per host, and ten of the 47 hosts publish a robots.txt Crawl-delay we are bound by (Arizona 30 s, Illinois 10 s, Missouri's document server 20 s), so no amount of impatience makes it finish sooner. A marathon job is also a job somebody has to remember is running; a nightly one is not.
_budget: --max-seconds 14400 is four hours, checked BETWEEN rounds and between states, never mid-fetch. When it expires the job logs what it did and exits 0, because a budgeted night is a success, not a failure — a red line in the morning digest should mean something broke. Nothing is lost at the boundary: every document already fetched is already committed, and the resume point is the ABSENCE of a "BillTexts" row, so tomorrow's run selects exactly what is left with no checkpoint file to go stale.
_pace: --parallel 4 states at a time, one connection per host inside each, >=1 s apart. 8 was tried and it exhausted Neon's connection pool inside ninety seconds; with the writes batched it would probably hold now, but that is a measurement someone should take deliberately rather than a number to raise on a hunch. Politeness is NOT the tunable half of this: the per-host serialisation, the robots.txt obedience, the Crawl-delay floor and the five-strike host drop all live in api/_lib/polite-fetch.ts and none of them is reachable from this manifest.
_scope: session_id >= 2023 (current and prior session), document_type='text' only — amendments are deferred, and turning them on adds 170,852 documents. NJ is excluded because it has its own job walking pub.njleg.gov back to 2010, and two processes on one host would break the one rule everything else here rests on. CA, OK, HI, TN, AK, DC and both PA hosts are not excluded here and do not need to be: they refuse us, the fetcher records the refusal, and the driver closes the state after one wholly-refused batch. Those states come from their own feeds in lane DP, not from this walker.
_order: Last of the livingston manifests by filename, after lv-text-delta, and that is the order the data wants: the delta is small, nightly and time-sensitive (it turns today's changed bills into text), while this is a long backfill with a budget. If the box has one slot the delta should have it. run-due's MAX_CONCURRENT of 2 means a night where both are due launches the delta first and defers this one to the next hourly catch-up, which costs this job a couple of hours out of a multi-week walk and costs the delta nothing.
